docRequirement: whats-new/2026-w22.md:108 binds us to a `MessageDisplay` hook event that "lets hooks transform or hide assistant message text as it is displayed". The shape is specified on hooks.md: it fires per batch of newly completed lines while an assistant message streams (once per message, `index` 0 / `final` true / whole message in `delta`, for `-p` and SDK runs) (hooks.md:1263, :1277); its input adds `turn_id`, `message_id`, `index`, `final`, `delta` to the common fields (hooks.md:1281-1294); its only output is `hookSpecificOutput.displayContent`, which "replaces the displayed text on screen. Display-only: the transcript and what Claude sees keep the original" (hooks.md:876, :1307-1311); it has no matcher support (hooks.md:270), no decision control (hooks.md:1313), and a 10-second default timeout instead of 600 (hooks.md:345, :1271).

- There is no display-interception channel to hook into. Assistant text reaches every surface as `text_delta`/`text_complete` on the main→renderer wire, each with exactly one text field: `SessionEvent` at packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:344-345. `SessionManager.processEvent` accumulates deltas (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:17679-17683) and batches them out through `queueDelta`/`flushDelta` (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:18496-18531); on `text_complete` it builds the persisted assistant `Message` with `content: event.text`, re-sends the same string, and persists (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:17687-17743).

divergence: The whole mechanism is absent, not misnamed and not narrowed. Missing, in order of depth: (1) the event name in `PluginHookEventName`, `PLUGIN_HOOK_EVENTS`, `AGENT_EVENT_CONTRACTS_V1` and `CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT_MAP`; (2) an emitter that fires per batch of completed lines with `turn_id`/`message_id`/`index`/`final`/`delta`; (3) a `hookSpecificOutput.displayContent` output field and its parse/projection surface; (4) the display-only property itself — our wire carries one text field that is simultaneously the rendered text and the persisted transcript entry (packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:344-345, packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:17687-17743), so even a correct hook result has nowhere to land that does not also rewrite the transcript, which hooks.md:1273 forbids. Secondary deltas: the 10 s timeout lowering and the matcher-silently-ignored rule have no row. What DOES exist is only the bookkeeping that says the event is unsupported — a named deferral (`plugin.deferred.event_message_display_unsupported`) that an importing plugin author sees instead of a hook that never fires.

blastRadius: Crosses a wire boundary AND a persistence boundary, so it is a risk trigger under AGENTS.md. (1) Wire: `SessionEvent` (packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:343) is the main→renderer/CLI protocol; every consumer of `text_delta`/`text_complete` is affected — apps/electron/src/renderer/event-processor/handlers/text.ts, apps/cli/src/index.ts:474/1944, and the dormant apps/webui + apps/viewer surfaces. Optional fields keep old clients working, but a client that ignores `displayDelta` shows the unredacted text, which for a redaction hook is the whole point failing silently. (2) Persistence: packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:17687-17743 builds and persists the assistant `Message`; the invariant to protect by test is that `session.jsonl` content is byte-identical with and without a MessageDisplay hook. (3) Type fan-out: adding a member to `PluginHookEventName` forces `PLUGIN_HOOK_EVENT_TO_AGENT_EVENT` (`satisfies Record<PluginHookEventName, …>`), and adding an `AGENT_EVENT_CONTRACTS_V1` row widens `AgentEvent`, which has ~195 referencing sites including packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts, packages/shared/src/automations/{utils,hook-command,hook-decision-contract}.ts and the renderer automations types (apps/electron/src/renderer/components/automations/types.ts:33). Any exhaustive switch over `AgentEvent` must be re-checked. (4) Stored automations: the `automations.json` v2 config is keyed by event name (packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/automation-management.ts:55-56 keeps its own literal `AGENT_EVENTS` list that will need the name too), so a new key is a forward-compatible config addition — old files stay valid, new files are unreadable by older builds. (5) Tests to update: packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/format-adapters.test.ts:3628-3648 and :3701 currently ASSERT the deferral and will fail by design; packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/hooks-automation.test.ts, packages/shared/src/automations/automation-system.test.ts and apps/electron/src/main/__tests__/session-event-message-parity.test.ts are the nearest covering suites. (6) Imported-plugin path: any Claude bundle whose `hooks/hooks.json` names `MessageDisplay` flips from "reported, never registered" to "registered and executed" — i.e. a plugin already installed today starts running a subprocess per streamed batch, under the existing plugin trust/integrity gate (packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:591-598). Per-batch execution on a hot streaming path is a latency surface the other 29 events do not have.
userImpact: Today: a user installs a Claude plugin that declares a `MessageDisplay` hook — the documented use cases are redacting API keys and internal hostnames out of assistant replies, and stripping markdown for a plain display (hooks.md:1265-1269). The install succeeds and the hook is silently inert: the adapter records `hook-event-MessageDisplay` / `plugin.deferred.event_message_display_unsupported` (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1308-1320) which travels to the Plugins page install outcome (apps/electron/src/renderer/pages/PluginsPage.tsx:294), and the assistant text renders exactly as the model produced it in both the desktop chat and the CLI. For a redaction plugin that is the failure that matters: the user believes secrets are being scrubbed from what is on screen and they are not. Nothing errors, nothing is logged at runtime, and the only signal is the deferral entry at install time. A plugin author writing against Claude's docs gets a reason code rather than an unknown-event warning, which is the intended half of the current behaviour.
